featured.title: Full Stack Web Development Bootcamp
featured.desc: Comprehensive full-stack engineering curriculum covering modern frontend web development, backend servers, relational databases, REST APIs, and authentication.
featured.learnt: End-to-end full-stack architectures, responsive design, React state workflows, asynchronous JavaScript, Node.js API development, SQL/PostgreSQL databases, and production deployments.

collections.name: Academic & Engineering Honors
collections.description: Competitive engineering design accomplishments and institutional recognitions at Toronto Metropolitan University.

items.title: 3rd Place — First-Year Engineering Student Design Competition
items.desc: Awarded 3rd Place overall for the project 'Sustainable Eco Powered House (SEPH)'. Selected as 1 of only 8 finalist teams across all first-year engineering sections at Toronto Metropolitan University.
items.learnt: Rapid multidisciplinary prototyping, sustainable energy integration, system trade-off analysis, and presenting technical engineering solutions to faculty and industry judges.

collections.name: Software Engineering & Systems Track
collections.description: Continuous specialized coursework in computer engineering, digital hardware, and modern full-stack development.

items.title: BEng in Computer Engineering (Software Engineering Option)
items.desc: Accredited Computer Engineering degree program with specialized Software Engineering concentration, bridging full-stack software development with low-level embedded hardware and digital silicon design.
items.learnt: Full-stack software architectures, algorithmic complexity, combinational & sequential digital circuits, microprocessor assembly interfacing, SQL relational database systems, and electronic circuit analysis.

courses.name: Object Oriented Eng Analysis and Design

items.title: 5th Semester: Database Systems & Microprocessors
items.desc: Advanced core semester focusing on relational database architecture, embedded microprocessor architectures, linear time-invariant systems, thermodynamics, and stochastic processes.
items.learnt: Database schema modeling (DDL/DML, normalization, indexing, query planning), microprocessor CPU architecture (instruction sets, registers, interrupt handling, peripheral interfacing), and frequency-domain LTI signal analysis.

items.title: 4th Semester: Algorithms & OOP Design
items.desc: Rigorous software engineering curriculum centered on asymptotic algorithm analysis, abstract data types, object-oriented design principles (GoF patterns), discrete structures, and analog electronic devices.
items.learnt: Trees, heaps, graph traversals (Dijkstra, BFS/DFS), dynamic programming, algorithmic space/time trade-offs, SOLID principles, design patterns (Singleton, Factory, Observer, Decorator), BJT/MOSFET amplifier analysis, and discrete logic.

courses.name: Object Oriented Eng Analysis and Design

items.title: 3rd Semester: Software Systems & Digital Systems
items.desc: Core computer engineering semester introducing formal software systems engineering in Java, hardware description with VHDL on Intel Quartus/ModelSim, RLC network analysis, and vector calculus.
items.learnt: Object-oriented program architecture in Java, combinational logic (multiplexers, ALUs, decoders), finite state machines (FSMs) in VHDL synthesized on FPGA boards, transient and sinusoidal circuit responses, and multi-variable differential equations.

items.title: 2nd Semester: Programming Fundamentals & Circuits
items.desc: Introduction to low-level procedural programming in C, DC/AC fundamental electric circuit analysis, multivariable integral calculus, and engineering economic evaluation.
items.learnt: Pointers, memory management, arrays, and structs in C; Kirchhoff's laws (KCL/KVL), nodal and mesh circuit analysis, Thévenin and Norton equivalents, op-amps, Taylor series, multiple integrals, and engineering project financial viability.

items.title: 1st Semester: Engineering Foundations & Mathematics
items.desc: Foundational engineering semester developing rigorous analytical problem solving, matrix algebra, differential calculus, Newtonian mechanics, and technical engineering documentation.
items.learnt: Vectors, matrices, eigenvalues/eigenvectors, systems of linear equations, limits, derivatives, optimization, Newtonian mechanics, equilibrium, work-energy theorem, and technical communication standards.

other.title: Sustainable Eco Powered House (SEPH) — 3rd Place Finalist
other.desc: Engineered an eco-powered sustainable housing model evaluated on renewable efficiency, architectural feasibility, and practical energy storage.
other.learnt: Sustainable design metrics, collaborative hardware engineering, and presenting under competitive judging criteria.
